mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25 percentage points over the next month, investors anticipate higher future inflation, which lowers real discount rates and drives up equity valuations, producing a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25pp in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day moving average of the prior month's returns (t-test p > 0.05) during the trigger period.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in PAYEMS (labor market tightness) coinciding with a decline in UNRATE (unemployment) suggests a tight labor market, which raises wage growth expectations and supports equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >5% while UNRATE falls by >0.5pp in the next quarter
regime_hint: Early stage of labor market recovery
failure_condition: Rank IC for the interaction < 0.05 over the 60-day horizon in all quarters with similar trigger conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in GDPC1 (real private consumption) above 2% of the prior month's value, persisting for two consecutive months, indicates robust consumer demand, which is associated with higher corporate earnings expectations and positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 grows by >2% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative or flat during the two-month GDPC1 acceleration period (mean p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (industrial production index) below 99.5 for two consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, which raises uncertainty and compresses discounting, producing a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 99.5 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (mean p-value > 0.1) during the contraction period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in CPIAUCSL (CPI) of at least 0.5% over three consecutive months, accompanied by a sustained rise in FEDFUNDS by 0.5%, creates expectations of higher future inflation and tighter policy, which typically precedes a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls by >0.5% for 3 months while FEDFUNDS rises by >0.5% over the same period
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 30-day average during the trigger window (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 5% for two consecutive months without a corresponding rise in PAYEMS, it signals a strengthening labor market that reduces wage growth expectations and compresses equity valuations, producing a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5% for two consecutive months and PAYEMS does not increase by >2% over the same period
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (mean p-value > 0.1) during the trigger window.

mechanism_narrative: A one-time monthly spike in HOUST (housing starts) above 1.5 standard deviations above its 12-month mean, followed by a return to trend, predicts a temporary boost in risk appetite and a positive S&P 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >1.5σ from its 12-month mean in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the 20-day average of the prior month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in RSAFS (retail sales) of at least 3% for three consecutive months indicates weakening consumer demand, which raises uncertainty and lowers equity valuations, producing a negative S&P 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls by >3% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 20-day average of the prior three months (mean p-value > 0.1).
